Subject: Console: short privacy callouts for data transfers & subprocessors — draft for sales

Team —

Acme legal asked for two one-line callouts we can surface in the Console and the hosted-API signup flow: (1) a very short note about cross-border transfers/SCCs, and (2) a short reassurance about subprocessors + live link to the subprocessor map. They want language that is sales-friendly, accurate, and consistent with the DPA.

I put together an initial draft (attached) with 3 options per callout — please review and flag anything that risks over-promising beyond the DPA. Goal: one 8–12 word line per callout for the UI card + a 1–2 sentence expand for the details panel.

Quick asks: 
- Legal (Kimberly): please confirm which of these are OK from a legal/DPA standpoint and any mandatory phrasing we must include (SCC/SSTD phrasing, references to data residency toggles).
- Product (Laura/Vanessa): pick the most concise options and call out where we might need tooltip hover text instead of full copy.

Attachments: console-privacy-snippets-v1.docx (short options + expand text)

Timeline: Acme would like this copy in the next 48 hours for an internal procurement sync.

Thanks —
Sean

Thanks Sean — I skimmed the doc and picked my top options inline. Two quick notes up front:

1) For the Console card we should prefer active language (e.g., “We protect and control cross-border transfers”) rather than legal-sounding phrases.
2) The expand text should reference the DPA page and link to the subprocessor map — avoid mentioning any specific third-party by name in the UI card.

Suggested picks (short/expand):
- Transfer callout (short): “Cross-border protections with SCCs and controls”
  Expand (1 sentence): "Our DPA uses EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and technical safeguards; see the DPA for details and per-region options."

- Subprocessors (short): “Subprocessors listed — up-to-date map”
  Expand (1 sentence): "We publish an up-to-date subprocessor list and notify customers in advance of material changes (see subprocessor map)."

Kimberly — any issues with the wording above? Also, Acme specifically asked whether the Console residency toggle enforces region-only storage for embeddings vs. logs — we should clarify retention/telemetry behavior in the expand text if needed.

I’ll mark the selected lines in the attached and create a single-file copy for the Console team once legal signs off.

Laura

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console: short privacy callouts for data transfers & subprocessors — draft for sales

Hi team —

Thanks for pulling this together. High level: the suggested short lines are fine if the expand copy accurately reflects the scope of the DPA and the technical controls we actually provide. A few legal constraints to keep front of mind: 

- Do not state that we "store data exclusively in region X" unless the customer has enabled a residency toggle and we have a contractual residency commitment.
- For EU transfers, reference "EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs)" or "appropriate transfer safeguards" rather than saying "SCCs guarantee" — avoid absolutes.
- Subprocessor messaging: we can say we "publish an up-to-date subprocessor map and provide advance notice of material changes," but we cannot promise individual customer approval rights unless in the contract.

I attached a short redline (DPA-redline-kimberly.pdf) with exact suggested phrasing for the expand panel. Preferred phrasings from legal: 

- Transfer short (legal-approved option): "Transfers protected by SCCs and technical safeguards"
- Transfer expand: "Our DPA includes EU Standard Contractual Clauses and additional technical/organizational safeguards; refer to the DPA for transfer mechanism specifics and region settings for your account."
- Subprocessors short: "Subprocessor list — current and transparent"
- Subprocessors expand: "We maintain a published subprocessor map and notify customers of material changes; customers can request data export or deletion under the terms of the DPA."

One operational note: product should not claim telemetry is deleted immediately unless we have a documented retention schedule tied to account settings. Vanessa/Laura — can you confirm what we communicate re: logs/telemetry vs. user data?

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachment: DPA-redline-kimberly.pdf

Sean / Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple clarifying questions from our procurement team before we sign off: 

1) For the "Transfers protected by SCCs" line — does that apply to embeddings and model input storage, or only to account metadata/backups? Can you point us to the DPA section that covers the exact data categories?

2) The "Subprocessor map" callout is helpful. Does Redwood notify customers at least 30 days before onboarding a new subprocessor that will have access to customer content?

3) We also need to confirm whether the Console residency toggle enforces both storage-at-rest and processing-in-region for inference requests, or only selects where backups are stored.

Please let us know the specific DPA and appendix references we can share with our legal team. We are happy to take a short FAQ line in the procurement doc that points to the DPA + subprocessor map if that simplifies wording.

Best —

Marta — thanks for the questions; appreciate the precision. Short answers and next steps below.

1) Scope of SCCs: Our DPA Appendix A documents data categories and transfer mechanisms. SCCs apply to customer content and any associated backups we store outside the EEA unless a residency toggle has been contractually enabled for your account. Kimberly attached the DPA redline with the exact appendix references — see the redline PDF.

2) Subprocessor notice window: Our standard practice in the DPA is to provide advance notice for material subprocessor changes; the notice period is 30 days for changes that increase access to customer content. We publish the subprocessor map and timestamp changes.

3) Residency toggle behavior: At present the Console residency toggle, when enabled via contract, scopes where persistent storage (including embeddings and backups) is stored. Real-time inference processing may still route to nearest capacity for latency reasons unless a dedicated deployment is provisioned; we can include a short clarifying sentence in the expand text. Vanessa — please confirm the exact sentence for the expand panel.

Next steps: 
- Kimberly will confirm the exact DPA appendix paragraph to reference (done: DPA, Appendix A, section 3 in the redline).
- I’ll send the single-file UI copy to the Console UX team after legal sign-off.
- I’ve uploaded the latest snippets and the subprocessor map to Drive and created a DocuSign envelope for the DPA amendment for Acme: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/to/DPA-ACME-0097

Attachments: subprocessors-map-may2027.csv (snapshot), console-privacy-snippets-v1.docx (final picks once legal OKs)
